q: How do you turn someone looking around into someone making things?
idea: The journey model is the page. Its four states of mind run left to right, the middle one is missing, and the real screens arrive to fill it.

beats.say: It starts with a look. “What does this do?”
beats.show: The first state of mind from the journey model, alone on the screen.

beats.say: Then, straight away, an empty box.
beats.show: The last state, far to the right. Between them, nothing: “Today journey largely skips over middle, goes from ‘learn capabilities’ to ‘create’”

beats.say: So we built the middle. “Can I try this for a something simple ...”
beats.show: A tool somebody else made slides into the gap, ready to run.

beats.say: “Can I trust this to be consistent for...”
beats.show: That tool's own page: how fast it was built, how often it has run.

beats.say: “How can this fit into my workflow for ...”
beats.show: The empty box again. This time the person knows what to put in it.

close: We map the change of mind first, then give each stage its place in the product.

q: How do you build for the expert without shutting out the beginner?
idea: One tool's page, never simplified. Each beat lights one more of its real buttons, so the same page gets deeper while nothing is added or removed.

beats.say: The team wanted engineers. The people arriving were not.
beats.show: The four kinds of builder, lined up by how much they know: “Tool consumer”, “Tool remixer”, “Tool Builder”, “Tool Chainer”

beats.say: Make it simple, and the engineers leave. “Favor enabling power users over simplifying for casual users.”
beats.show: One tool's page, whole and dense, everything dimmed.

beats.say: So nothing came out. It was put in order. First: run it.
beats.show: Only the Run button is lit. The consumer stops here, and that is fine.

beats.say: Then read how it works, and change it.
beats.show: Use spec lights. It opens the conversation with this tool's spec already filled in. The remixer and the builder go this far.

beats.say: Then take it with you.
beats.show: Get API and Get code light last. The whole page is on, and it is the page from beat two.

close: We keep the depth, and build the way up to it.
imgs: The page, with its real buttons

q: How do you make the first visit worth a second?
idea: The same front page three times: visit one, visit two, visit ten. The page does not change. What the person reaches for does.

beats.say: Visit one. You run a tool somebody else made. It works.
beats.show: The front page; a hand goes to one of the ready-made tools. A small counter reads 1.

beats.say: You leave. That was the plan.
beats.show: The page empties. The bet, in its own words: “which will require more than one visit”

beats.say: Visit two. You come back with a problem of your own.
beats.show: Same page, counter at 2. The hand goes to Remix on the tool that was closest.

beats.say: You change it until it fits.
beats.show: The conversation opens with that tool's description already written in.

beats.say: Visit ten. You start from the empty box.
beats.show: Same page, counter at 10. The hand goes to the box it ignored the first time.

close: We design the first ten minutes to earn the next visit, not to close the sale.

q: How do you fix the onboarding when the onboarding isn't the problem?
idea: The old flow drawn as one line, starting at an empty box. Everything we built appears to the left of where that line began.

beats.say: The ask: “Cleaning up onboarding”. Six weeks. No redesign.
beats.show: The scope of work, as it was written.

beats.say: We walked the product. It began at an empty box.
beats.show: The old flow, one line: write a prompt, build, run. Nothing before the first step.

beats.say: “If you weren’t here to walk me through it, I would have dropped off already.”
beats.show: The line holds. A person stands to its left with no way onto it.

beats.say: The trouble sat before the first screen. Nobody knew what to ask for.
beats.show: The blank space left of the line, held.

beats.say: So the way in became product: something to try, something to change, someone to ask.
beats.show: Three real screens arrive in that space, in order, and join the line.

close: We answer the brief by finding the problem underneath it.

q: How do you serve the person who knows what they want, and the one who doesn't?
idea: The two flows as two lines down the screen, one for the builder and one for the looker. Each decision moves one line in front, until they meet.

beats.say: Two people arrive. One has a job to do. One is curious.
beats.show: Two lines begin side by side: the create flow and the explore flow.

beats.say: Every page can only lead with one of them. “is this intent and curiosity? how are we grabbing intent”
beats.show: The lines cross a page and tangle.

beats.say: We chose. “Intent > Curiosity”
beats.show: The builder's line moves in front. The bet, as written.

beats.say: Then held to it. On a tool's page: “‘similar’ before ‘other’ because ‘Intent’ before ‘curiosity’”
beats.show: The same choice, small, on a real page: similar tools above the maker's other tools.

beats.say: The curious are not turned away. They are given a way to become builders.
beats.show: The looker's line runs through a tool, through Remix, and joins the builder's.

close: We choose who comes first, and then hold to it on every page.
imgs: The round where it was argued

q: How do you decide what not to build?
idea: Subtraction. A wireframe crowded with everything that was proposed; each beat one thing is lifted off, with the note that removed it, until one box is left.

beats.say: Everything on the table at once.
beats.show: The crowded round: search, categories, free runs, a place to browse.

beats.say: Search? “there is no point in replacing create with a far lower quality action”
beats.show: The search bar lifts off. The note stays where it was.

beats.say: Free runs? “no point in getting a person to “run” if they dont want to commit”
beats.show: The free Run goes.

beats.say: A home for the merely curious? “at the moment we dont need to design for that”
beats.show: The browsing page goes.

beats.say: What is left is the one act that matters.
beats.show: One box, and the tools beside it: the real front page.

close: We keep the product about one act, and say no to the rest out loud.

q: How do you say what you are in a few words?
idea: The headline slot of the real front page, and nothing else. Each candidate sits in it at full size, then the note that killed it, then the next.

beats.say: “AI-tools. For every Job.”
beats.show: Set where the headline goes. Then the note: “these arent AI tools though. They are tools made with AI.”

beats.say: “There’s a tool for that.”
beats.show: Replaces it. Then the note: “EWverything might not preexist”

beats.say: “Generated tools.”
beats.show: Holds, alone, for two rounds of wireframes.

beats.say: “Generated Code.” “AI for Software.”
beats.show: Quick ones, each a little wrong, each gone.

beats.say: “Outsource to AI.”
beats.show: It stays. The rest of the real front page fades in around it, with the line under it: “The code to bring your words to life.”

close: We write the headline as a design problem, until the product fits inside it.
imgs: The one on the front page

q: How do you get someone to give up a habit that works?
idea: A search bar. The page starts as the habit itself, a search and a row of one-off tools, and those tools turn into the cards on the front page.

beats.say: You need two PDFs merged. You search.
beats.show: A search bar, and under it the one-off tools from the first bet's slide.

beats.say: You pick the first result. It works. You close the tab.
beats.show: One tool opens, does its job, and is gone.

beats.say: That is who we were up against. “one google search away”
beats.show: The tab closes again and again, a different tool each time.

beats.say: So this is not sold as something new. “a new way of completing an existing behavior to users, not a new behavior”
beats.show: The scattered tools slide into one grid: the real front page.

beats.say: And the next job is already there.
beats.show: The hand that came for one tool moves to the one beside it. That was the test.

close: We design against what people already do, not against an empty space.

q: How do you get a team to see its product as a stranger does?
idea: One newcomer's walk through the old product, told only in the notes the team wrote. The flow is the stage, and each step speaks one note.

beats.say: Home. “I don’t really know what types of thing I can build with CodeWords”
beats.show: The old flow's first box, with one note beside it.

beats.say: A prompt. “what are integrations?”
beats.show: The line moves one step. The next note.

beats.say: A build. “Do I just sit and wait?”
beats.show: The line stops here for a while.

beats.say: A run. “What is this page for?”
beats.show: The last step.

beats.say: The team wrote every one of these.
beats.show: Pull back: the whole flow, covered in their notes.

close: We get the team to find the problem themselves, so the fix is theirs too.
imgs: The old flow, with the team's notes
